title: Thailand 2-Week Itinerary 2026 — The Complete Route (Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Pai, Krabi, Samui) | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A realistic 2-week Thailand itinerary: 3 days Bangkok + an Ayutthaya day, 3 in Chiang Mai + 2 in Pai, 3 on the Krabi islands, then 3 on Koh Samui or Phangan — day-by-day plans, travel times, costs and where to stay. Plus what two weeks buys you over ten days.
keywords: thailand 2 week itinerary, two weeks in thailand, thailand 14 day itinerary, bangkok chiang mai pai krabi samui, thailand travel plan two weeks, slow thailand route
ogDesc: City, mountains, a Pai detour and two coasts in 14 days: Bangkok + Ayutthaya, Chiang Mai + Pai, Krabi islands, then Samui or Phangan. Day-by-day plan, travel times, costs and where to stay.
intro: Two weeks is where Thailand really opens up. You keep the classic first-timer trio — Bangkok, the north, the islands — but you stop rushing: a day trip to the Ayutthaya ruins, a detour up to Pai, a dive or cooking day, and a second beach so the coast isn't a single blur. This is the complete route, day by day, with travel times, rough costs and where to stay.
quickAnswerHtml: The best 2-week Thailand itinerary keeps the classic route but slows it down: 3 days in Bangkok with an Ayutthaya day trip, 3 in Chiang Mai plus 2 in Pai, then two beaches — 3 on the Krabi/Andaman islands and 3 on Koh Samui or Phangan. Add a dive or cooking day. Two or three short domestic flights tie it together.
quickAnswerH2: The perfect two weeks in Thailand, in one line

blocks.html: The short version: fly into Bangkok for 3 days plus a day trip to the Ayutthaya ruins. Fly north to Chiang Mai for 3 days, then wind up to Pai for 2 slow ones. Fly south to Krabi for 3 days of limestone and island-hopping, then hop to a second beach — Koh Samui or Phangan on the Gulf, or a quiet Andaman island — for the final 3. Two or three short flights carry the load; book them early. Want to cut it to ten days, or trade a leg? See the alternative routes below.

blocks.html: Start where almost everyone lands. With two weeks you can give Bangkok three unhurried days and still fit the Ayutthaya ruins without feeling squeezed. Base near the BTS/MRT (Sukhumvit or Silom) so the traffic never owns your day, and hit the big temples early before the heat.

items: Day 1: ease in — a riverside temple or two, then Chinatown (Yaowarat) for street food after dark. See the Grand Palace & temples guide
Day 2: the big hitters — Grand Palace, Wat Pho's reclining Buddha, Wat Arun across the river; a rooftop bar at sunset. Skip-the-line and combo tickets on the Bangkok attractions & tickets page
Day 3: a day trip to Ayutthaya — cycle between brick temples and stone Buddhas at the old capital, then back for a market evening. See Bangkok to Ayutthaya for train vs tour

blocks.title: Two weeks buys you the slow version
blocks.html: Two weeks means you can afford the slow version of Ayutthaya: take the cheap train up in the morning, rent a bicycle, and don't try to see every ruin. Three or four of the big ones with time to sit in the shade beats a checklist rush.

blocks.html: A one-hour flight lands you in a completely different Thailand: cooler air, a moated old town, hundreds of temples and mountains on the doorstep. Chiang Mai is where the trip changes gear. See how to get from Bangkok to Chiang Mai (flight vs sleeper train).

items: Day 4: wander the old-town temples on foot (Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh); sunset at Doi Suthep above the city. Tickets and tours on the Chiang Mai attractions page
Day 5: a morning at an ethical elephant sanctuary (choose no-riding, observation-first camps), then a Thai cooking class in the afternoon
Day 6: the Sunday Walking Street or Saturday market, cafés (Chiang Mai is Thailand's coffee capital), or a day up Doi Inthanon — then pack light for Pai

blocks.title: Where to stay in Chiang Mai
blocks.text: The old town puts you walking distance from the temples, markets and cafés.

blocks.html: This is the leg ten days doesn't have room for. Pai is a laid-back mountain town three hours northwest of Chiang Mai, reached by a famously winding road — 762 curves — through pine hills. It's hot springs, a small canyon at sunset, rice-field cafés and evenings on a walking street. Go slow; that's the whole point. See Chiang Mai to Pai for the minivan (and the curve warning).

items: Day 7: the minivan up in the morning (motion-sickness tablet if you're prone), settle in, then Pai Canyon for sunset over the ridgelines
Day 8: a lazy loop — hot springs, a waterfall, the Land Split fruit-wine stop and rice-field cafés, then the night walking street for food

blocks.title: The Pai road is genuinely twisty
blocks.html: The Pai road is genuinely twisty. Sit up front, take a tablet 30 minutes before, and it's fine. Renting a scooter in Pai is popular but only if you already ride confidently — the mountain roads and gravel are not the place to learn.

blocks.title: Where to stay in Pai
blocks.text: Riverside bungalows and rice-field guesthouses just outside the walking street are the classic Pai stay.

blocks.html: Back down the mountain to Chiang Mai, then fly south (usually a quick Bangkok connection) to the Andaman coast, where limestone cliffs drop straight into turquoise water. Base in Ao Nang or on car-free Railay. This is your beach-and-boat stretch, and with three days you can add a dive. See the Krabi tours & tickets and our island-hopping guide.

items: Day 9: arrive, settle into Ao Nang or take the longtail to Railay for cliffs and calm beaches
Day 10: the classic island-hopping day — Phi Phi, the Hong Islands or the 4-Islands tour by speedboat
Day 11: a dive or snorkel day (Krabi is a good place for a first try-dive), or a slow day at Emerald Pool and the hot springs inland

blocks.title: Where to stay in Krabi
blocks.text: Ao Nang for restaurants and ferry access; Railay for cliffs and quiet.
Days 12–14: a second coast (Samui or Phangan)

blocks.html: The two-week payoff: a second, different beach instead of one coast on repeat. Cross to the Gulf for Koh Samui (easy, resort-y, direct flights out) or its quieter neighbour Koh Phangan — greener, slower, famous for its full-moon night but lovely the rest of the month. Not sure which? Read Koh Samui vs Koh Phangan. Prefer to stay Andaman? Swap in a quiet island like Koh Lanta from the island-hopping guide.

items: Day 12: travel over (ferry + flight, or the Krabi-side boats to the Gulf), arrive and do nothing — a swim and an early dinner
Day 13: the island's best — a waterfall and viewpoint on Samui, or a longtail to a hidden bay and Thong Nai Pan on Phangan
Day 14: a final slow beach morning, then fly home from Samui (or ferry back to the mainland for your flight)

blocks.title: Where to stay on Samui
blocks.text: Chaweng and Bophut for restaurants and easy transfers; the quiet south and west for calm.

blocks.text: Two weeks vs ten days: what the extra days buy you

blocks.html: The ten-day route hits Bangkok, Chiang Mai and one island and does it well. The extra four days aren't about cramming in more places — they're about breathing room: a Pai detour, a real dive or cooking day, and a second coast so the beach half of the trip has variety. Here's how to reshape it either way.

blocks.caption: How to adapt the two-week route to your pace and taste

Add a dive or extra beach day

Krabi + Phi Phi + Koh Lanta, then Samui + Phangan on the Gulf
Skip the north — see island-hopping guide

blocks.title: Know before you go (for this route)

items.title: Book the domestic flights early
items.text: Bangkok–Chiang Mai and the leg south to Krabi are cheap booked weeks ahead and pricey last-minute. Carry-on only speeds up the budget airlines.

items.title: The Pai road takes a morning
items.text: Three hours of curves each way, so treat Pai as an overnight, not a day trip. Take the minivan up rested and early, and a motion tablet if you're prone.

items.title: Andaman vs Gulf in wet season
items.text: If you travel May–Oct, the Gulf islands (Samui, Phangan) often stay drier than Krabi. Put the drier coast at the end so you finish on good weather. See best time to visit below.

items.text: Data makes Grab, maps and ferry bookings effortless across all five stops. See our eSIM guide.

faq.q: Is two weeks too long for Thailand?
faq.a: Not at all — two weeks is close to ideal. It covers the same core as a 10-day trip (Bangkok, the north, the islands) but with room to slow down: a Pai detour, a dive or cooking day, and a second beach. If anything, most people wish they had this long rather than ten days.

faq.q: What is the best 2-week Thailand route?
faq.a: Bangkok (3 days, plus an Ayutthaya day trip) → Chiang Mai (3) → Pai (2) → Krabi (3) → Koh Samui or Phangan (3). It gives you city, culture, mountains and two contrasting coasts, with two or three short domestic flights tying it together.

faq.q: How much does a 2-week Thailand trip cost?
faq.a: Excluding international flights, budget travellers can do two weeks on roughly US$40–60 a day, mid-range around US$80–150 a day, and comfortably more at the top end. Domestic flights, island tours, a dive course and nicer hotels are the main variables. See our Thailand daily budget guide for a full breakdown.

faq.q: Should I add Pai, or skip it?
faq.a: Add it if you have the full two weeks and want a change of pace — Pai is slow, green and mountain-cool, and two nights is the sweet spot. Skip it if you're tight on time or don't enjoy winding roads; the three-hour minivan each way is the main cost.

faq.q: When is the best time to do this itinerary?
faq.a: November to March (cool, dry season) is best across all five stops. April is very hot but includes Songkran. In the May–October wet season, favour the Gulf islands (Koh Samui, Koh Phangan) over the Andaman coast, and put that drier coast at the end of the trip.
